sections.body: Study 19 is an external source review of two user-supplied community posts and seven tracker screenshots. One trader reports every taken trade was logged: 55 cumulative trades over four weeks, then 100 over seven weeks. Browser headers attribute both posts to Christopher Thornton, with date labels Aug 5 and Aug 28 (edited); the year is not visible. We have no raw ledger or independently authenticated fills. These are overlapping cumulative samples, not 155 independent observations. Abacus has documented the source; our empirical analysis is planned for a future run.

sections.body: Strategy value_area_first_touch_fade · proposed · decision date 2026-10-07. In a balanced/rotational market, the source describes selling from value-area high (VAH) toward point of control (POC), or buying from value-area low (VAL) toward POC. Developing/current-session value areas, D-shaped profiles, early touches and VWAP are possible context variables. The first post reports 40 such fades among 55 trades, but no fade-only win rate; its overall rate cannot be assigned to this strategy. The author says they do not enter at POC. Later discussion separates balanced-day reversals from trending-day continuation. No operational continuation setup is provided, so that is a separate future branch. No Abacus trading or risk-increase recommendation follows from this source review.

sections.body: The author reports no support for the idea that same-type aligned value areas (for example current VAH aligning with prior or overnight VAH) improve success relative to unlike-type alignment. No sample counts, effect estimate or exact comparison rule were provided. Preserve this as a negative external claim, not a controlled Abacus rejection. The later VWAP rate falls to 67%, and A-grade falls to 86%; high early rates did not persist unchanged. The source’s direction-neutrality conclusion lacks direction-specific outcome rates. D-shape, first-touch and grade associations have unspecified confounding and no joint-filter data.
sections.title: Negative and inconclusive source claims

sections.body: Post 1 describes standardizing trades at 1:1 R:R. Post 2 says letting winners run improved profitability despite lower win rate; it reports an average 1:2 R:R for the last eight A-grade trades and suggests partial profits at 1:1 with a runner. These are the author’s descriptions, not verified realized returns or a tested exit comparison. A follow-up author comment says they only trade 1:1 and tracked how far A grades would run, so the 1:2 figure may describe potential excursion rather than realized payoff. There is no payoff series, mean win/loss, fees, slippage, sizing or P&L amounts. Reported partial fills in micros matter for capacity. A 69% win rate cannot establish positive net expectancy, nor does the streak summary justify increasing risk. Psychological comments describe the author’s experience; they are not statistical proof of a coin-flip process.
sections.title: Trade management and execution limits

sections.body: Future work will first obtain a raw timestamped ledger if available and define reproducible causal profiles, balanced/trending state, D-shape, touch counting, grade and VWAP rules before outcome inspection. Pin immutable Bhishma releases and available_at timing. Prespecify chronological development and untouched holdout periods. Compare first-touch balanced VA fades with later-touch opportunities under the same execution policy, then assess shape and VWAP separately; report coverage and retain negative findings. Freeze entry/fill, stop, timeout, POC/fixed-R/partial-runner exits, unadjusted prices, costs, contract rolls and overlapping-position treatment. Report net R, drawdown, MFE/MAE and session-clustered uncertainty, with all missing/ambiguous events retained. Separate discretionary taken-trade audits from all-eligible market-event research. Our own analysis has not been run.

sections.body: One trader, a short evolving seven-week process, self-selected opportunities, overlapping groups and cumulative samples. Grades may be retrospective; many denominators and all individual timestamps are missing. We cannot estimate joint-filter performance, incremental VWAP benefit, a weekday edge, fill capacity, drawdown or net profitability. Rounded percentages and arithmetic consistency do not authenticate the record. Changes in market mix, exits and the author’s skill prevent attributing changes to one filter. The screenshots’ rate pies should be read as labeled values rather than valid shares of a whole.
sections.title: Interpretation limits

sections.body: Two pasted posts and seven supplied screenshots were reviewed on 2026-10-07. The first post is linked by the later post; its webpage was not retrievable with the web tool. Existing signed-in browser tabs confirmed Christopher Thornton as author, the follow-up URL, and date labels Aug 5 / Aug 28 (edited). No year was visible. Selected author comments clarify discretionary grading and uncertainty over realized versus potential R:R. Cam Narayan is acknowledged as a teacher, not the author. Full post bytes are retained privately with checksums. Selected screenshots are preserved without editing, and public tables/downloads are transferred from the saved source-review tables. The completed review has frozen settings, input hashes, source/environment identities and an integrity manifest. New analysis or interpretation requires a new run.

report.summary: An external evidence study and proposed first-touch VAH/VAL-to-POC strategy. Two overlapping snapshots, seven source charts, reported rates and sample counts, contrary evidence, execution gaps and a plan for future independent Abacus analysis.
